title: Verbs to know through the end of Momente Lessons 1–3
scope: Core lesson verbs, essential formula verbs, and a separately labelled reference inventory of verbs in the covered classroom instructions and optional Module 1 material. Full forms for recognition-only verbs are not a requirement to memorize all those paradigms.

priority_guide.core: Use actively in personal-profile, family and language conversations. See each note for whether the complete paradigm is explicitly tested.
priority_guide.phrase: Master or recognize the stated fixed expression; full forms are reference.
priority_guide.classroom: Recognize the task/context meaning. Full forms are optional reference, not end-of-Lesson-3 conjugation targets.

source_key: KB = owned Momente A1 coursebook; AB = owned Momente A1.1 workbook. Page references are printed page numbers, not PDF page indices. The glossary is the official English glossary. Module 1 includes the review, magazine, business and exam sections after Lesson 3.

entries.example: Ich bin 28 Jahre alt. Wir sind verheiratet.
entries.translation: I am 28 years old. We are married.
entries.notes: Memorize all six forms. Lesson 1 introduces singular/formal forms; Lesson 2 completes the plural. Use sein for age, profession and marital status: bin Single / bin geschieden / bin verheiratet. The es form is supplied as reference.

entries.english: to be called; to have the name
entries.example: Wie heißt du? Ich heiße Sara.
entries.translation: What is your name? My name is Sara.
entries.notes: du heißt, with no extra s; ich heiße, with ß. Do not write ich heißt. The plural forms are consolidated in the module grammar table.

entries.example: Woher kommt er? Er kommt aus der Schweiz.
entries.translation: Where is he from? He is from Switzerland.
entries.notes: Use kommen aus + place for origin. Contrast wohnen in + place for residence.

entries.english: to learn; to study a language
entries.example: Sie lernt Deutsch. Wir lernen Deutsch.
entries.translation: She is learning German. We are learning German.
entries.notes: Use lernen for learning German. University subjects use studieren in the taught profile patterns.
Master spelling your name and recognizing Buchstabieren Sie bitte. Full regular forms are useful reference; the course grammar tables do not separately test this whole paradigm.
entries.source: Glossary L1 ex6; KB p155; AB pp24–25.

entries.example: Wo wohnt ihr? Wir wohnen in Berlin.
entries.translation: Where do you live? We live in Berlin.
entries.notes: Residence: wohnen in + town. Wo? asks where; Woher? asks origin.
In these profile examples leben in and wohnen in both describe residence. Also master Ich lebe allein and Wir leben zusammen.

entries.example: Lebt ihr zusammen? Ja, wir leben zusammen.
entries.translation: Do you live together? Yes, we live together.
entries.notes: The glossary lists zusammen|leben; the lesson teaches leben … zusammen as a relationship-status pattern. Memorize this pattern. A full general theory of separable verbs is beyond Lesson 3.
entries.source: Glossary L2 ex2; KB pp16–17; AB pp10–12.

entries.example: Habt ihr Kinder? Wir haben zwei Kinder.
entries.translation: Do you have children? We have two children.
entries.notes: Irregular du hast and er/sie hat: no b. Also learn habe keine Kinder and habe einen Job / eine Stelle as complete patterns.

entries.example: Sie arbeitet als Ärztin. Ich arbeite bei X-Net.
entries.translation: She works as a doctor. I work at X-Net.
entries.notes: Keep the extra e: du arbeitest, er/sie arbeitet, ihr arbeitet. als introduces the role; bei introduces the employer.

entries.example: Was machst du beruflich? Ich mache eine Ausbildung.
entries.translation: What do you do for a living? I am doing vocational training.
entries.notes: Required patterns: Was machst du / machen Sie beruflich? and eine Ausbildung / ein Praktikum machen. Regular present endings.

entries.example: Was studierst du? Ich studiere Medizin.
entries.translation: What do you study? I study medicine.
entries.notes: Use studieren for a university course/subject. German language study is usually Deutsch lernen in these lessons.

entries.example: Welche Sprachen sprichst du? Ich spreche Deutsch und Englisch.
entries.translation: Which languages do you speak? I speak German and English.
entries.notes: Only du and er/sie/es change the stem e to i: sprichst, spricht. ihr sprecht keeps e. Learn all six forms.

entries.example: Wie geht es dir? Es geht.
entries.notes: Required now: Wie geht's? = Wie geht es?; Wie geht's dir/Ihnen?; Es geht. Here es is the subject, so geht stays singular even with Ihnen. Other forms are reference, not a Lesson 3 movement-verb requirement.

entries.example: Ich glaube, Lara ist Toms Schwester.
entries.translation: I think Lara is Tom's sister.
entries.notes: Required now: Ich glaube, … as a short opinion/guessing frame followed by a normal statement. Learn the chunk; the other forms are reference. No dass-clause is needed.

Optional business-module phrase. Freut mich is short for Das freut mich. Do not use these bare reference forms to invent reflexive sentences; sich freuen has its own pronouns and is not a Lesson 3 grammar target.
entries.source: AB pp22–23; AB transcript track1_31, visually inspected.

entries.notes: Recognition/request chunk in the module listening test only. The modal verb system and conjugation mastery are taught later; these six forms are reference.
entries.source: AB transcript track1_28, visually inspected; module test AB p20.

entries.english: to tick; to mark with a cross
entries.notes: Recognize the instruction; full forms are reference. Separable an appears at the end.
entries.source: Glossary L1 ex3; KB p12; AB pp7,9.

entries.notes: Recognize sagen/sagt and the classroom instruction Sagen Sie. No separate conjugation requirement.
Classroom instruction. Separable an; du siehst and er/sie sieht are reference, not core L3 targets.
entries.source: KB pp11,13–14; AB p87 upper L3 section.

entries.example: Hören Sie und sehen Sie das Bildlexikon an.
entries.translation: Listen and look at the picture dictionary.
entries.notes: Recognize the base verb inside ansehen instructions. The general e→ie conjugation pattern belongs to later study; forms here are reference.
entries.source: KB p13 ex7; KB module pp24–26.

entries.notes: A frequent classroom instruction; recognize it immediately.
Instruction for connecting words, pictures or sentences. Extra e in du/er/ihr forms is reference.
Recognize in classroom instructions. Extra e in du/er/ihr forms is reference.
Instruction vocabulary, with regular reference forms.
Recognize weiß/wissen in task questions. Irregular present paradigm is supplied for reference only; it is not required by the L1–3 grammar tables.
Recognize as an instruction. du ergänzt has no added s after z.

entries.english: to repeat aloud after a model
entries.example: Hören Sie und sprechen Sie nach.
entries.notes: Instruction: repeat the model aloud. The sprechen stem changes are core in L3; the separable verb paradigm here is only reference.
Recognize the instruction. Also used in question-and-answer task descriptions.
Instruction vocabulary; full forms are reference.
Recognize the separated instruction Ordnen … zu. Distinct from ordnen, to put in order.
Recognize this classroom instruction. No separate conjugation mastery target.
Frequent classroom instruction. Also recognize Wie schreibt man das? in the module exam task; man uses the er/sie/es form.
Instruction recognition now; du liest and er/sie liest are reference, not a new L3 core stem-change target.

entries.english: to put in order; to sort
entries.notes: Recognize the instruction.
Recognize the instruction, including comparing your answers with a partner.
From the du/Sie partner game. Strong forms are reference only.
entries.source: Glossary L1 ex8; KB p156 upper L1 section.

entries.notes: Frequent instruction. Extra e in du/er/ihr forms is reference.
entries.source: KB p156 L1 partner activity; AB pp12,21.

entries.notes: Recognize the instruction. Full reference forms are provided, not required as a separate core drill.
entries.source: AB p9 ex15b; KB module p24.

entries.english: to solve; to complete an exercise
entries.notes: From partner-task directions. du löst, with no extra s after s.
Appears as a learning-goal label. Recognition only. Reflexive uses and their pronouns are not a Lesson 3 conjugation requirement.

entries.english: to say goodbye; to take leave
entries.notes: Appears in the learning goals with sich. Bare forms are reference; the reflexive verb system is beyond this scope.
Recognize both sich vorstellen (introduce oneself) and eine Person vorstellen (introduce someone). These separated forms are reference; memorize the classroom chunks.
entries.source: KB p11 learning goals; KB pp18,158; AB pp19,24.

entries.translation: to state where someone is from
entries.notes: Learning-goal vocabulary rather than an active conjugation target.
entries.source: KB p11 learning goals; KB p28 headings.

entries.notes: Occurs in the module communication summary heading. Master the actual phrases Entschuldigung and Wie bitte?; no full bitten paradigm drill is required.
Learning-goal label with sich. Master Danke as the L1 phrase. Reflexive constructions and these bare forms are reference only.
Instruction/heading vocabulary.
Frequent task question. du passt, without an extra s.
Instruction in Schon fertig? optional work. ich sammle is the standard short form; ich sammele is also possible.
Game instruction. Separable vor; no general separable-verb system is required now.
Appears in L2 partner-game instructions, and role-play instructions later in the module.
entries.source: KB p156 lower L2 section; AB p22.

entries.notes: Guessing-game instruction. Irregular du rätst / er rät are reference only.

entries.english: to arrange; to put in order
entries.translation: Put the items in order and write them down.
entries.notes: Base ordnen occurs in the L2 quick test; zuordnen is separately listed for matching tasks.
Recognition of the literal task meaning only. The opinion pattern Ich finde … belongs to Lesson 4 and is excluded here.
entries.source: AB p11 ex4; KB p158 directions.

entries.notes: Recognize the separated instruction lesen … vor. Forms supplied as reference.

entries.example: Hören Sie und klatschen Sie mit.
entries.notes: Pronunciation-task instruction. Full paradigm is reference only.
Encountered as betont in a pronunciation task. Recognize the meaning; passive grammar is not required.

entries.english: to draw; to move a game piece
entries.notes: Also used for drawing a business card in the module. No core conjugation requirement.
entries.source: KB p156 L2 game; AB p23.

entries.notes: Instruction. ich würfle is the common short form; ich würfele is also possible.
Recognize in game directions. bekommen means get/receive, not English become.
Instruction vocabulary.
entries.source: KB p157 L2 activity; AB pp20,24.

entries.notes: Recognize fehlt in number games and fehlend in instructions.
Occurs in L2 partner activity and is listed under Magazin 01 in the glossary. Task recognition, not an additional core conjugation drill.
entries.source: KB p157 ex6c; glossary Magazin01; KB pp24–25.

entries.translation: Do you not understand a word?
entries.notes: Useful recognition and classroom phrase. Also Ah, jetzt verstehe ich in the module listening test. Full paradigm is reference.
entries.source: KB pp158,192; AB transcript track1_28, visually inspected.

entries.notes: Extra-practice instruction. Full reference paradigm only.
Classroom task vocabulary.
entries.source: KB p20 ex3; module KB p24.

entries.translation: You are planning a family celebration.
entries.notes: Only the optional Schon fertig? task requires recognizing this meaning. Do not add general future tense study.
Frequent instruction, not a separate active paradigm requirement.
entries.source: KB p21 ex7b; module KB p24.

entries.example: Geben Sie den Steckbrief Ihrer Partnerin.
entries.translation: Give the profile to your partner.
entries.notes: Instruction on the L3 partner page. Strong present forms are reference only; dative objects are not a required grammar system yet.

entries.english: to suppose; to make a guess
entries.notes: Communication-summary label. The actual learner phrase is Ich glaube, … . Full forms are reference.

entries.english: to hang up; to put up
entries.notes: Optional magazine-project instruction. No general separable-verb mastery requirement.

entries.english: to know; to be familiar with
entries.notes: Optional magazine task recognition. Distinguish from wissen (know a fact), but no full new verb drill is required.
Optional magazine task instruction.

entries.english: to film; to record a video
entries.notes: Optional magazine-project instruction.

entries.english: to research; to look up information
entries.translation: Look up information on the internet.
entries.notes: Optional magazine-project instruction.
Optional surname-project question. Extra e in du/er/ihr forms is reference.
Also occurs in L2 and L3 workbook word-building instructions; earliest taught content AB p12. Classified as classroom recognition.
Module review instruction. Separable ein; no extra s after the stem s.

entries.english: to vary; to change a model
entries.notes: Audio-training instruction. Keep the two consecutive i letters in variieren.
Module speaking-test instruction. Irregular reference forms only; no general separable-verb system required.
Optional business task instruction.
Optional business task. du nimmst / er nimmt are reference; active conjugation comes later.
Module exam-preparation instruction. Stem-changing forms and dative grammar are recognition only.
Module exam-preparation instruction.
Module writing-test instruction; auf is part of the phrase, not a separable prefix.
Recognize this opinion prompt in classroom tasks. The full paradigm is reference, not a separate Lesson 3 conjugation requirement.
